summary_1line: Virtues depart from Prahlada when Behaviour is lost; Dhritarashtra explains righteous conduct, and Bhishma begins a tale on the power of Hope.

image_candidates.scene_text: Radiant personifications of Truth, Good Deeds, Might, and Prosperity emerge one after another from Prahlada’s body and depart into the distance.
The goddess of Prosperity, shining and lotus-bearing, rises from Prahlada’s body as the king watches in fear and astonishment.
Armored King Sumitra races through a wild forest with bow drawn, chasing a wounded deer that bounds far ahead with an arrow in its flank.
